answer: Each identity joins one grove registry, posts a 40-credit bond, and files a single relic record: a hash of prior work bound to its own wallet key. A public panel checks the relic against the registry; a duplicate or key mismatch burns the bond. The spiral fee makes the k-th identity from one wallet cost 40+10k credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 5,045,000 credits. A rented-relic ring fails because a borrowed relic still carries its owner's key and trips the mismatch check. One honest identity posts 40 once and reclaims it after a clean epoch.
